title: Dating and Romance
goal: Make or clarify a date invitation, express interest or refusal, discuss expectations, and close the encounter honestly.

runs.text: Would you like to go out with me?
can make romantic interest clear. A coffee invitation alone can be ambiguous: it might mean a date, friendship or another purpose. Ask when you need to know.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Would you like to get coffee with me Saturday?

turns.en: Would you like to get coffee with me Saturday?

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: Do you mean as a date?

turns.en: Do you mean as a date?

runs.text: Yes, if you're interested.

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: I'd like that. Saturday afternoon works for me.

turns.en: I'd like that. Saturday afternoon works for me.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Great. How about two at the café?

turns.en: Great. How about two at the café?

runs.text: I'd like that
accepts the idea.
I'd love to
expresses stronger enthusiasm.
I was hoping you'd ask
can express playful interest when that is what you want to convey. Clear time and place still matter; Chapter 12 supplies scheduling support.
We should meet up sometime
shows an interest in meeting, but does not confirm a date or romantic intention.
Maybe. Let me check
is also unconfirmed. A possible reply is
Sure. Let me know
, rather than treating it as a definite yes.

rows.text: I can't on Saturday. How about Sunday?
The proposed time does not work, but you offer another.
Thanks, but I'm not interested in a date.
A clear refusal of the romantic invitation.
I like you as a friend.
You are not participating in dating at present.
No. I don't want to go out.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Would you like to go out Friday?

turns.en: Would you like to go out Friday?

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: Thanks, but I'm not interested in a date.

turns.en: Thanks, but I'm not interested in a date.

runs.text: Okay. Thanks for being clear.

blocks.caption: Decline the right thing · Alex & River

runs.text: A refusal does not need an excuse or an alternative day.
I already have plans

only explains availability; it may leave romantic interest unclear. If you mean no to dating the person, a clearer refusal can express that meaning. If someone declines, acknowledge the answer rather than continue as though it were an invitation to negotiate.
Begin with a short greeting from Chapter 1. A compliment such as
You look great
is optional, and
Thank you
is enough to accept it.
At the café

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: It's good to see you. I'm a little nervous.

turns.en: It's good to see you. I'm a little nervous.

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: Me too. What do you like to do outside work?

turns.en: Me too. What do you like to do outside work?

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: I like hiking and live music. How about you?

turns.en: I like hiking and live music. How about you?

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: I like cooking. I've been trying new recipes lately.

turns.en: I like cooking. I've been trying new recipes lately.

runs.text: What do you like making?

blocks.caption: Talk on the date · Alex & River

runs.text: I'm a little nervous
names a feeling without requiring the other person to solve it. A follow-up can come from an interest they actually mention.
You can ask about expectations:
Are you looking for a relationship?
Ask about their goal.
I'm looking for something serious.
Describe interest in a committed relationship.
I'm keeping things casual for now.
Describe a less committed approach; explain what casual means to you if it matters.
I'm not sure yet.
Give an uncertain answer.
I'd rather not discuss my past relationships tonight.
Keep a topic private.
Casual
serious
, and
exclusive
can need a conversation about expectations.
We're not exclusive
means you have not agreed to date only each other; it does not define every other expectation automatically.

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: I'd like to kiss you. Is that okay?

turns.en: I'd like to kiss you. Is that okay?

runs.text: Not right now.
Okay.

blocks.caption: Express affection or a boundary · River & Alex

runs.text: You can also answer
Yes, I'd like that
or
No, I don't want to
I'd like to take things slowly
describes a preference for the pace. These words give each person a way to express what they want in the moment.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Thanks for today. I had a good time. I'd like to see you again.

turns.en: Thanks for today. I had a good time. I'd like to see you again.

turns.speaker: River

runs.text: I had a nice time too, but I'm not feeling a romantic connection.

turns.en: I had a nice time too, but I'm not feeling a romantic connection.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Okay. Thanks for telling me. Take care.

turns.en: Okay. Thanks for telling me. Take care.

blocks.caption: End with the intention clear · Alex & River

runs.text: If both want another date,
I'd like that. Let's find a day next week
begins the next plan.
Maybe, I'll let you know
leaves it open. Avoid inventing an enthusiastic promise merely to finish the conversation smoothly.
How are you getting home? — I'm taking the bus
can discuss departure.
I need to head out
is a closing signal. Chapter 10 supplies other endings.
All roles below are invented adults. Rehearse both people alone, or alternate roles with a partner.
Invite someone to coffee. They ask whether it is a date. Your role means a date, and they are interested. Clarify, accept and propose Saturday at two.
Change the response: they are busy Saturday but interested Sunday. Rehearse an alternative. Then change the meaning again: they do not want a date. Give a clear refusal and acknowledgment.
On a date, ask about interests. Your partner likes cooking and music. Follow up on one. Supplied answer:
I like making pasta
or
I like jazz
Your role is unsure about a relationship goal. Answer
Are you looking for something serious?
without giving a false certainty.
Someone asks to kiss you. Your role wants to wait. Say so; give the other person's acknowledgment.
At the end, one person wants another date and the other does not. Rehearse the complete exchange with a clear answer rather than a fake plan.
Hide Study. Make a four-turn invitation or ending in which the reply differs from the first model.
Sample possibilities
Yes, I mean as a date. — I'd like that. — How about Saturday at two?
I can't Saturday. How about Sunday?
versus
I'm not interested in a date. — Okay.
What do you like cooking? — I like making pasta.
I'm not sure yet. I'm still figuring that out.
Not right now. I'd like to take things slowly. — Okay.
I'd like to see you again. — Thanks, but I'm not feeling a romantic connection. — Okay. Take care.
Check:
Was interest, uncertainty or refusal clear? Did the next turn respond to the answer given? Did you distinguish availability, relationship expectations and personal boundaries?
